mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns, so low rates predict positive 5-day returns due to compressed discount rates and accommodative monetary policy.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market tightness condition, defined as the unemployment rate exceeding 6.0%, signals a potential economic slowdown that increases equity risk aversion, leading to negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 6.0%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.3% monthly growth) signals a stagflationary risk, which increases equity market volatility and leads to negative 20-day returns.
failure_condition: In instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 0.3% monthly growth, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by GDP growth above 3% annualized and unemployment rate above 5.5%), the S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative due to increased risk of policy tightening and economic overheating.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 3% annualized and UNRATE > 5.5%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3%) signals an increased risk of monetary policy tightening, which leads to negative 20-day returns due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 0.3%, 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns, so high housing starts predict positive 20-day returns due to strong consumer spending and economic growth.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1400, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising industrial production (INDPRO > 105.0) and rising employment (PAYEMS > 144000 thousand) signals a strong economy, leading to positive 20-day returns due to robust corporate earnings and consumer confidence.
failure_condition: In instances where INDPRO > 105.0 and PAYEMS > 144000, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns due to sustained low interest rates supporting equity valuations and economic growth.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
